sections.title: 第3問 長文読解
sections.instructions: 英文を読んで、各問いに最も適切なものを1〜4から1つ選びなさい。
passage: [1] Last spring, Yuna, a first-year student at a high school in Shizuoka, noticed something strange. Many students threw away umbrellas, bags, and headphones when they were only a little broken. “Most of these things could be used again if someone fixed them,” she thought.

[2] She talked to her science teacher, Mr. Ono, about her idea. He told her about “repair cafés,” events where people bring broken things and volunteers help them repair the items for free. The first repair café was held in the Netherlands in 2009, and now there are thousands of them around the world. Yuna decided to start one at her school.

[3] At first, it was not easy. Only three students came to the first meeting, and none of them knew much about repairing things. So Yuna asked some local people for help. Mr. Kato, a retired engineer, and a woman who runs a small sewing shop agreed to teach the students once a month.

[4] Six months later, the repair café had become popular. Now, every Friday after school, students line up in the science room with their broken things. The members do not simply fix the items for them. Instead, they show the owners how to repair the items by themselves. “If you learn how to fix something, you will take better care of it,” Yuna says.

[5] The club has repaired more than 200 items so far. However, Yuna believes that the most important thing is not the number of items but the change in people’s thinking. “Before, we thought new things were always better. Now many of us <u>think twice</u> before we throw something away.”

items.q: 問1　Why did Yuna start thinking about repairing things?〔3点〕
choices: Because she visited a repair café in the Netherlands.
Because she saw many students throw away things that were only slightly broken.
Because her own umbrella broke on a rainy day.
Because her teacher asked her to make a new club.

items.q: 問2　What problem did Yuna have at first?〔3点〕
choices: The teachers did not allow her to use the science room.
Local people complained about the noise.
Few students joined, and they did not know much about repairing things.
The club did not have enough money to buy tools.

items.q: 問3　下線部 think twice の意味に最も近いものを選びなさい。〔3点〕
問4　What do the members of the repair café do instead of simply fixing the items?〔3点〕
choices: They sell new items to the owners at a low price.
They show the owners how to repair the items by themselves.
They send the broken items to Mr. Kato's company.
They throw the items away and recycle them.

items.q: 問5　Why do the members do so?〔3点〕
choices: Because people who learn how to fix something will take better care of it.
Because the teachers do not allow students to touch other people's things.
Because the members do not know how to repair things well.
Because the club does not have enough tools.

items.q: 問6　本文の内容と合うものを1つ選びなさい。〔5点〕
choices: Yuna thinks a change in people’s way of thinking is more important than the number of repaired items.
The club has repaired fewer than 100 items so far.
The first repair café in the world was started by Mr. Ono.
Mr. Kato and the owner of a sewing shop teach the students every week.

sections.title: 第4問 長文読解
sections.instructions: 英文を読んで、各問いに最も適切なものを1〜4から1つ選びなさい。
passage: [1] For most of human history, people could look up at night and see thousands of stars. Today, however, about 80 percent of the world’s population lives under skies that are polluted by light, and more than one-third of all people can no longer see the Milky Way from where they live. Scientists call this problem “light pollution.” It is caused by artificial light from streetlights, buildings, and advertising signs that shines up into the sky instead of onto the ground, where it is actually needed.

[2] Light pollution may seem like a minor issue compared with air or water pollution, but researchers have found that it can have serious effects on wildlife. Many animals depend on natural patterns of light and darkness. For example, young sea turtles hatch on beaches at night and find their way to the ocean by moving toward the brightest horizon, which is usually the sea reflecting the light of the moon. Near brightly lit hotels and roads, however, many of them crawl in the wrong direction and die before they reach the water. Similarly, every year, large numbers of birds that travel at night are confused by city lights and crash into tall buildings.

[3] Humans are affected, too. Our bodies produce a hormone called melatonin when it is dark, and this hormone helps us sleep. Studies suggest that being exposed to bright light at night, especially the blue light from screens and some LED lamps, can reduce the amount of melatonin we produce. As a result, people may have trouble falling asleep, and in the long run, their health may suffer.

[4] The good news is that light pollution is one of the easiest kinds of pollution to reduce. Unlike chemicals in rivers or plastic in the ocean, light disappears the moment it is turned off. Some towns have already taken action. They have replaced old streetlights with new ones that point downward and use warmer colors, and they have asked stores to turn off their signs after closing time. In some of these towns, the changes have not only made the night sky darker but also greatly reduced the cost of electricity.

[5] Some people worry that darker streets will lead to more crime. However, the evidence for this is not clear. Several studies have suggested that well-designed lighting, which lights only the places people actually use, can keep streets safe while wasting less energy. Experts say that the goal is not to remove all lights but to use <u>“the right light, in the right place, at the right time.”</u>

[6] Some areas have even turned their dark skies into an attraction. Places that have been recognized as “dark sky parks” attract tourists who want to see the stars clearly, and this has brought new business to small towns. As more people learn about the problem, the stars may one day return to the skies above our cities.
（注）artificial 人工の　hatch ふ化する　horizon 地平線・水平線　hormone ホルモン　melatonin メラトニン　be exposed to ～ ～にさらされる

items.q: 問1　According to the passage, what causes light pollution?〔4点〕
choices: The light of the moon reflected by the sea.
Large numbers of tourists visiting dark sky parks.
Artificial light that goes up into the sky rather than onto the ground.
Smoke from factories that blocks the light of the stars.

items.q: 問2　Why do many young sea turtles die near brightly lit hotels and roads?〔4点〕
choices: The lights wake them up too early in the day.
The heat from the lights makes the sand too hot.
The artificial lights lead them away from the sea.
The noise from cars frightens them.

items.q: 問3　What does the passage say about melatonin?〔4点〕
choices: It is produced mainly when we are exposed to blue light.
LED lamps help our bodies produce more of it.
It is a chemical that pollutes rivers and oceans.
Bright light at night may reduce the amount of it, making it harder to fall asleep.

items.q: 問4　Why does the writer say light pollution is “one of the easiest kinds of pollution to reduce”?〔4点〕
choices: Because new streetlights are cheaper than old ones.
Because the pollution stops as soon as the lights are turned off.
Because the government has banned advertising signs.
Because most people do not use lights at night.

items.q: 問5　Which of the following is true according to the passage?〔4点〕
choices: Some towns have cut their electricity costs by changing their lighting.
Experts say all streetlights should be removed to protect wildlife.
Dark sky parks have caused small towns to lose business.
Research clearly shows that darker streets always lead to more crime.

items.q: 問6　Which is the best title for this passage?〔2点〕
choices: The Hidden Costs of Bright Nights and How to Reduce Them
Why Cities Need More Light at Night
How Sea Turtles Find the Ocean

items.q: 問7　下線部 “the right light, in the right place, at the right time” が表す考え方として最も適切なものを選びなさい。〔5点〕
choices: 野生生物を守るため、夜は街の明かりをすべて消す。
明かりをすべてなくすのではなく、必要な場所に、必要な時だけ、適切な明かりを使う。
眠りをさまたげないよう、街灯をすべて青い光のLEDに取り替える。
犯罪を防ぐため、街全体をできるだけ明るく照らし続ける。
